title: Small local tests make an existing infinity reflector accessible
statement: Use accessible infinity categories and universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and coherent mapping spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be accessible, let $\mathcal E\subset\mathcal C$ be a replete full subcategory with inclusion $i$, and suppose a mapping-space adjunction $L:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal E:i$ is already given with $L$ left adjoint, meaning a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(LX,e)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(X,ie)$ of mapping-space bifunctors. Let $T$ consist of all arrows $f$ of $\mathcal C$ for which $iL(f)$ is an equivalence. Suppose there exists a small set $S_0\subset T$ such that every object $Z$ for which $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for each $(A\to B)\in S_0$ has the same property for every $(A\to B)\in T$. Then $\mathcal E$ is accessible and the endofunctor $iL:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ is accessible. Accessibility of a functor between accessible infinity categories means preservation of small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some regular $\kappa$; no existence of an adjoint is asserted here.
